history.blurb: Ben Jorgensen donated 17 acres of land in West Gunnison near the Gunnison River to the City of Gunnison for the purpose of creating a long-term care facility for seniors.

The Gunnison Home Association (GHA) was incorporated on April 23. The City transferred the donated land to the organization. Fundraising began for construction of the Health Care Center, and groundbreaking took place on October 15.
The 54-bed Health Care Center was completed. The first residents were received on October 11, and the facility was formally dedicated on December 12.
The Iva Lehman Solarium was added to the Health Care Center, funded entirely through donations and built without incurring debt.
A workshop and storage facility was constructed in memory of Clarence Lehman, again completed without debt.

The Mildred R. Brown Addition, a 4,200-square-foot expansion and remodel of the original building, was completed and dedicated on November 24, funded largely by community donations and a major contribution from Mildred R. Brown.
Ownership of the Health Care Center and six acres of land was transferred to Gunnison County, debt-free, following voter approval to support the facility with a property tax levy.
A Master Plan was developed for 4+ acres of the remaining property to be used for assisted and independent senior living.
Construction of The Willows Assisted Living facility was completed on Lot A at a cost of over $2 million. Funding came from GHA reserves, grants, contributions, and a $500,000 mortgage.

Ownership of The Willows and three adjacent lots was transferred to Gunnison County. The GHA also developed and opened the Gunnison RV Park for senior campers, with a grand opening celebration in September.
GHA donations supported projects benefiting seniors, including facility upgrades, transportation, and funding for local organizations totaling $36,500.
GHA contributed $28,635 to The Willows, the Volunteer Fire Department, Senior Scoops, and the City of Gunnison’s Senior Wing at the Rec Center.
GHA funded additional staff and activities at the RV Park, which grew to 6,040 camper nights in 2019. Efforts continued toward creating accessible independent living units for seniors.
COVID-19 delayed the start of the season, but GHA maintained safe activities at the RV Park. Camper numbers decreased, though short-term stays helped offset losses.
The first cycle of GHA’s new grant program awarded $64,225.16 to local organizations supporting seniors, including The Willows, Hospice & Palliative Care, and others.
GHA awarded $52,050.00 in grants to community programs supporting seniors.
GHA awarded $51,745.00 in grants for 2024 programs and discussed concerns over the closure of the memory care wing at the Health Care Center.

GHA granted $52,345.92 to senior-focused organizations. In memory of Board Member Bill Knowles, GHA funded $172,000 to replace the Willows' fire suppression sprinkler system, using funds previously set aside for Gunnison Valley Health.
The Gunnison Home Association celebrates 52 years of service to seniors in the Gunnison Valley, continuing to promote activities and services that enrich their lives.
